verdict: Avoid new unsecured or single-mill exposure in Kolkata jute; lend only to mills with confirmed PCSO price realisation, low raw-jute inventory leverage and demonstrated bonus/wage cover.
title: Kolkata jute mills & products: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A jute mill buys raw jute, spins and weaves it into sacking, hessian and B Twill bags, and sells largely to government PCSO orders plus some domestic and export buyers. **Cash is made or lost on the spread between raw jute cost and the notified bag price, not on volume.** The West Bengal Labour Minister has asked the Centre to re-notify August 2026 B Twill prices because the notified rate did not reflect mills' raw jute procurement cost, and to apply the July 2026 rate to July PCSO quantities [3]. So when a proposal lands, check which price notification the order book is billed at; if the mill is holding August-rate invoices, ask what differential it expects and whether it has written confirmation.

## Where value and cash sit now
**Working capital is seasonal and swings with raw jute price versus MSP** [8][10]. Rating reports show fund-based utilisation as low as around 7% over 15 months to May 2025 for one entity [10], and nil utilisation over 12 months for another [8] — meaning strong mills are under-borrowed while weak mills are stretched. Raw jute prices are high, and Cheviot is shifting to the domestic market and new value-added export products in response [1]. **The stress is real: mills are struggling to meet wages and puja bonus** [2][3]. Note the peer read: Crisil sees sales volumes rising 15% and a twenty percent rise in domestic demand with softer raw jute lifting margins [6][7] — that is a rating-agency view, not a Kolkata mill result, and it sits against the local wage and pricing evidence.

## The growth opportunity
**Pursue mills with a confirmed PCSO order book, a 30-day manufacturing and inspection window, and value-added product lines** — the direction Cheviot is taking [1]. The Labour Minister's proposal for a minimum 30-day window from PCSO placement is the structural fix to watch [3]. Avoid single-mill, single-buyer sacking converters with no value-added line and no bonus reserve. Kolkata-specific mill-level data is thin in these sources; lean on first principles and the peer read.

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the price notification, not the order.** Take monthly: raw jute purchase register versus MSP, PCSO inspection status, wage and bonus payment proof, and stock statement reconciled to jute price. Covenant that drawing power resets on each notification. **The macro backdrop is tight — repo at 5.5%, raised from 5.25%, RBI tightening [D] — so price working capital for a higher rate.**

## Early-warning signs
- **Bonus or wage delay past the puja date** [2][3] -> stop fresh limits, review all drawings.
- **August-rate invoices unresolved** [3] -> ask for the differential claim in writing.
- **West Bengal GST -1.3% Apr-to-date versus India +6.1%** [D] -> tighten local collateral cover.
- **Exports -13.6% Apr-to-date in USD** [D] -> cap export-receivable limits.
